* fix: trace router.param callbacks at their origin

Parameter callbacks bypassed layer instrumentation, so their errors were
either missing from the error channel or attributed to a downstream error
handler that merely forwarded them.

Trace each executed parameter callback and share error publication and
deduplication with layer handlers. Expose the actual callback as handler
and its parameter name as param while retaining the associated Layer and
request-scoped matched route pattern. This identifies the origin without
modifying shared Layer metadata or Route.dispatch.

Preserve parameter caching, callback arguments, routing signals and promise
semantics. Skip tracing context allocation when there are no subscribers.
Document the context fields and cover synchronous and asynchronous errors,
concurrent requests, nested router copies and bound tracing stores with
24 regression tests.

Refs #213.

Validation: npm test (792 passing), npm run lint, npm run test-types.

* fix: preserve tracing context and error attribution

Publishing asyncStart directly skipped its bound AsyncLocalStorage stores,
leaving asyncEnd subscribers without the expected context. Errors raised
before tracing was enabled or during route matching could also be blamed
on handlers and mounted routers that merely forwarded them.

Run async completion publication through asyncStart.runStores so bound
stores remain active through asyncEnd without scheduling additional work.
Keep the existing order of error propagation and lifecycle events.

Record error identities at router boundaries, matching failures and error
handler entry. Track them per request even when their origin was untraced,
so a late subscriber cannot misattribute a forwarded error. Newly created
replacement errors are still published at their origin, and the existing
registered symbol preserves deduplication across router copies.

Document these semantics and add 33 tests for bound stores, late
subscriptions, incoming errors and malformed URLs in mounted routers.

Validation: npm test (825 passing), npm run lint, npm run test-types.

* refactor: share parameter callback invocation

Use one callParam helper for traced and untraced callbacks so exception,
promise rejection and deprecation handling cannot drift between them.
Keep completion notification optional and preserve tracing's end event
in finally. Resolved promises still require an explicit next() call.

Cover resolved promises without tracing and correct the rejection test
to exercise the parameter callback itself.
